subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Mitral Stenosis, Eisenmenger, Cardiomyopathy and Valve Anticoagulation

steps.tx: Narrowing of the mitral valve from rheumatic scarring, the commonest heart lesion in pregnancy worldwide, is **rheumatic mitral stenosis**. Fixed outflow cannot accommodate the rise in cardiac output and heart rate of pregnancy. Pulmonary oedema threatens especially at peak output and after delivery.
steps.say: Rheumatic mitral stenosis cannot accommodate pregnancy output rises and threatens pulmonary oedema.

steps.tx: Functional breathlessness grading predicting tolerance is the **NYHA class**. Classes one and two usually complete pregnancy safely, three and four carry major risk. Class is reassessed every trimester as output rises. A woman breathless on climbing one flight sits in class two; breathless at rest is class four.
steps.say: NYHA class predicts pregnancy tolerance, with classes three and four carrying major risk.

steps.tx: Cardiac output peaks at twenty eight to thirty four weeks and again immediately after delivery, the **peak cardiac output** danger windows. Autotransfusion from the contracted uterus floods the circulation after birth. Most decompensations cluster at these two moments. About 500 millilitres autotransfuse with each postpartum uterine contraction emptying into the circulation.
steps.say: Peak cardiac output windows in late pregnancy and just after delivery cluster decompensations.

steps.tx: Reversed shunt with cyanosis from pulmonary vascular disease, forbidding pregnancy, is **Eisenmenger syndrome**. Maternal mortality reaches thirty to fifty percent, mostly postpartum. Termination is discussed honestly, and contraception is life preserving. Even modern series report death in about a third, concentrated in the first week after delivery.
steps.say: Eisenmenger syndrome forbids pregnancy with maternal mortality up to fifty percent.

steps.tx: Heart failure appearing in the last month or first five months after delivery without other cause is **peripartum cardiomyopathy**. Bromocriptine and standard failure therapy aid recovery in many. Future pregnancy counselling depends on whether function normalises. Left ventricular ejection fraction under 45 percent near term or within five months postpartum supports the diagnosis.
steps.say: Peripartum cardiomyopathy appears around delivery and future pregnancy depends on recovery.

steps.tx: Mechanical valves demand anticoagulation balancing valve thrombosis against fetal harm, the **prosthetic valve** dilemma. Warfarin protects valves best but causes embryopathy in the first trimester. Heparin protects the fetus but thromboses valves more, while low molecular weight heparin with level monitoring is the common compromise, balloon mitral valvotomy relieves severe stenosis in pregnancy, endocarditis prophylaxis follows dental and delivery indications, ergometrine is avoided for its hypertensive surge, and mWHO classification grades every lesion from low to forbidden risk.
steps.say: The prosthetic valve dilemma balances warfarin embryopathy against heparin valve thrombosis.

steps.tx: Splitting the fused mitral commissures with a balloon during pregnancy is **balloon mitral valvotomy**. It relieves severe stenosis refractory to medical therapy, ideally after twenty weeks. Radiation shielding protects the fetus during the brief procedure. Relief is judged by the gradient across the valve falling and symptoms easing within days.
steps.say: Balloon mitral valvotomy relieves refractory severe stenosis ideally after twenty weeks.

steps.tx: Ergometrine is avoided in cardiac disease because its vasoconstriction surges pressure, an **avoid ergometrine** rule. Oxytocin by slow infusion replaces it for the third stage. Even oxytocin boluses drop resistance dangerously and are given slowly. Syntocinon given as a slow infusion of 10 units over hours is the usual cardiac third stage regimen.
steps.say: Ergometrine is avoided in cardiac disease and oxytocin is given by slow infusion.

steps.tx: The modified WHO system grading lesions from safe to pregnancy forbidden is the **mWHO risk classification**. Class four includes Eisenmenger and severe stenosis with symptoms. It structures counselling, surveillance intensity and delivery planning for every lesion. Class one and two lesions need no intervention beyond surveillance; class four is pregnancy not advised.
steps.say: mWHO classification grades every cardiac lesion from safe to pregnancy forbidden.
